answer: The cheesemaker wheels each cheese into the cellar, stamps its rind and writes the stamp, the milk and the date in the cellar book. When the applicant claims a seat, the desk reads the stamp against the book. A cedar cheese bought at market fails the book: at the falcon of the rind the stamp must match the cellar's own wheel, and market cheese carries no stamp at all. Faking a wheel means keeping a dairy for a year, buying milk and rennet and paying 8,600, and the jetty book is read at every fair, so a cheese whose stamp was never entered is thrown to the pigs.
